title: The cut-corner button
summary: Your reference, adapted: every primary action now has one cut corner, set in capitals at weight 600 — the heaviest your type spec allows — slightly larger and tighter, with no arrow. The four options are shown side by side on graphite, paper and the red plane.
story: The page's primary action — Request a System Audit — gets a signature shape of its own: sharp, with one cut corner.
motion: Hover deepens the fill; the keyboard focus ring is drawn inside the cut so it is never clipped.
addressed: Cut corner: yes — one 45° chamfer, bottom-right, sharp everywhere else. Technical and ownable, and it keeps the no-rounded-corners rule.
All caps: the buttons were already in capitals; they are now weight 600 at 14px with tighter tracking, so they read punchier, like your reference.
Not bold 700 (option D): your type spec caps UI text at 600, and at 700 the button starts to look generic.
No arrow (option C): the cut corner already reads as “go”, which is closest to your reference. Option B keeps the arrow if you miss it.
Only the primary action gets the cut; the small outlined nav button stays square, so the shape always means “the main thing to do here”.
notes: Applied site-wide via the kit's .ac-btn; specimen page shows A–D.
